chapter: Zulu, Nice and the Punch Miller incident
title: Mayor Morrison, the keys to the city and the Zulu experience
summary: Rose says Morrison appreciated Armstrong as jazz's prime representative.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: When Louis came back at Zulu, Mayor Morrison gave him Keys to the City. Sure. I mean, the thing is. How do you think Morrison viewed Louis? I mean, what was his?

Oh, well, he considered him to be a great delight and that he was a big asset to the city, the fact that Louis was from here. I mean, Shep appreciated Louis, you know. Um, he could, Shep wasn't the kind of a guy that would have thought of Louis as a commercial asset for the city. But he was just happy that he was from here.
He was very conscious of the fact that jazz was born here and that Louis was its prime representative.

Of course, as far as Keys to the City is concerned, you know, the mayor's got a pile of these things. Oh yeah. And he gave me a bunch of them to give away in France during the bicentennial. So, it wasn't Shep, but I mean.
So anyway, Louis was happy with the Zulu experience though.
Oh yeah, I would think so. Yeah. He was kidding for a day. Yeah. No, I was, I was.
